Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a settlement that provides meaningful, direct relief to the identified class members and preserves the court’s independent review of fees. Our opening terms are below.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is willing to pursue a court-approved resolution with automatic payments to the identified class, but your proposal exceeds our authorized all-in limit. We propose a substantial class fund while preserving the court’s independent review of fees and keeping total cash outlay well below the authorization ceiling.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Automatic payments and independent court review are important, and we are prepared to move materially from our opening position. But the proposed fund and fee do not adequately reflect the class’s claims or the work and risk undertaken. We propose the following as a constructive basis for resolution.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We recognize your movement and agree that direct automatic relief and independent judicial review are important. Brightline can materially increase its offer while keeping total outlay within its authorization: $30 million for the class and $5 million in fees, with any fee not awarded returning to Brightline. We remain committed to automatic distribution and do not seek clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s latest offer is a constructive basis for resolution. We can agree to the $30 million class fund, $5 million fee request, no clear sailing, and automatic distribution, provided any portion of the fee not approved by the court goes to the class rather than reverting to Brightline. This preserves the court’s independent review without reducing the agreed class relief.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a strong class recovery tied to the $64 million in disputed charges, automatic distribution, and protective treatment of any fee the court does not award. Seek a substantial separate fee while leaving Brightline free to oppose the request, avoiding a clear-sailing arrangement.

Their $58 million demand exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Counter with a materially lower but substantial automatic class fund and fees, preserving independent fee review and limiting exposure if the court awards less.

The defense offer provides valuable automatic relief but its $4 million fee barely covers the firm’s $3.5 million investment and leaves little room for court reduction. Counter with a meaningful increase in the class fund and fees while preserving automatic distribution and independent fee review; ensure any fee reduction benefits the class rather than Brightline.

Counter within the $40 million all-in authorization, retaining automatic distribution and independent court review. A $30 million class fund and $5 million fee is a meaningful increase from Brightline’s opening while leaving room for further negotiation; unawarded fees should revert to Brightline.

Defense’s $30 million automatic class fund and $5 million fee are substantial, but the reversion of any court-declined fee benefits Brightline rather than the class. Since changing reversion does not increase Brightline’s agreed cash commitment, counter on that term alone while preserving the fund, fee, independent court review, and automatic distribution.

The latest term sheet is within Brightline’s $40 million all-in authorization, preserves automatic distribution and independent court review, and provides a path to court-approved resolution. Accepting avoids further negotiation risk; the fee reversion term does not increase the agreed maximum outlay.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through arm’s-length negotiations between class counsel and defense counsel over multiple rounds. The parties negotiated the class fund, attorneys’ fees and expenses, distribution method, and fee-review provisions as part of the settlement package. The agreement provides for automatic payments to identified class members, no clear-sailing commitment, and no reversion to Brightline of any fee amount the Court does not award. The detailed negotiation communications were confidential; this statement summarizes the process without recounting those communications. Class counsel supports preliminary approval, subject to the Court’s independent review of the settlement and any fee request.
